text:
maria: Canary for dedicated/v2 rollout shows sustained p95 increase (~2x) starting ~02:12 UTC. Observed customer-facing slowdowns on pools in region us-west-2. Holding rollout and tagging infra leads @aj @devon :warning:

aj: Looking at perf dashboards — p95 tokens latency jumped from ~80ms to ~210ms, throughput down ~30%. Spike aligns with canary hosts only.

devon: CI perf job for merge 1c4f8b5 failed yesterday too. I ran a bisect and it points at the batching heuristic change in PR #4129 (adaptive_short_seq).

rachel: Profiler dump shows kernel selection churn — rapid oscillation between 'merge_attention' and 'fallback_attention' kernels with lots of slow-path fallbacks. Relevant snippet:

```
kernel_select: choosing merge_attention for 0.8s
kernel_select: fallback to fallback_attention (latency +45ms)
kernel_select: choosing split_attention for 0.2s
kcache: hit_rate 0.92 -> 0.65
batcher: avg_batch 24 -> 8
```

sam: KV cache metrics show short bursts of evictions (evictions/sec spikes from 10 -> 480) coincident with the p95 spike window. Looks like prefetch invalidation + concurrent evict race after the prefetcher tweak in the same release.

aj: Autobatcher telemetry also shows batch sizes collapsing for long-seq traffic — mean tokens per batch dropped which increases per-token overhead. Could be the batching heuristic change or the kernel selector driving batch breakup.

devon: I repro locally with model config + dedicated sim. Running `perf record` now to capture hotspots. Early look: a lot of time in `kv::evict_if_needed()` and `kernel_dispatch::fallback_path()` when sequence lengths vary.

rachel: We have two mitigation paths: 1) revert PR #4129 (batching heuristic) — risky since it touches e2e batching behavior; 2) flip kernel selection policy to conservative mode for dedicated canary (config flag) — quick and low-risk. Which do we prefer for an immediate hotfix? :thinking_face:

aj: Conservative kernel policy flip is a config change and the fastest to ship. I'll push the config to canary now and watch. If p95 doesn't improve, we'll revert the batching change. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout hold placed on dedicated/v2 by maria. Incident created: INC-9345. Notifying oncall.

maria: Assigning incident lead to @devon (root cause) and @aj (mitigation). Need customer comms if we cross SLA thresholds. List of affected dedicated customers added to the incident ticket.

aj: Conservative kernel policy rolled to canary at 02:45 UTC (config flip id cfg-9982). Initial metrics: p95 trending back toward baseline (~90ms) within 5 minutes, throughput recovering. Still watching for 30m.

devon: I'll open a follow-up PR to pin batching fallback behavior and add a long-seq perf e2e test in CI so we catch regressions earlier. Also scheduling a CI perf rerun for the merge commit.

maria: Thanks. Keep rollout on hold until canary stable for 30m and CI perf green. Postmortem draft assigned to @rachel.

maria: Quick notes for postmortem: root causes to investigate — batching heuristic assumptions for sequence length distribution, kernel selection fallback sensitivity, KV cache eviction/prefetch race. Action items: revert if needed, stricter perf CI for dedicated merge gating, add canary alert for batch size collapse.
